III. Salary
A. Salary Processing Procedures of the University
After newly appointed personnel complete the appointment procedures→ the
Personnel Office prepares and issues a Personnel Action Notice → the Cashier Section,
Office of General Affairs (prepares the employee cash remuneration roster) → the Office
of General Affairs (reviews and affixes its seal on the roster) → the Personnel Office
(reviews and affixes its seal on the roster) → the Second Section, the Budget, Accounting
and Statistics Office (consolidates accounting items and calculates the total expenditure)
→ the President or an authorized representative grants final approval → the Third
Section, Budget, Accounting and Statistics Office (prepares accounting vouchers) → the
Cashier Section, Office of General Affairs (issues National Treasury checks for payment)
→ the Budget, Accounting and Statistics Office (verifies the official seals on the checks)
→ the Office of the President (verifies the President’s seal) → the Cashier Section →
funds are remitted through financial institutions and credited to the designated
accounts.
B. Principles for Salary Point Levels and Monthly Salary by Academic
Rank
8

C. Principles for Salary Determination and Salary Advancement
1. Principles for Salary Determination
(1) Newly appointed faculty members shall have their salaries determined in
accordance with their appointment rank, commencing from the first grade of
base salary for the respective rank.
(2) Faculty salaries are calculated on a monthly basis and paid monthly. Newly
appointed faculty members must complete the check-in procedures on or before
August 1 (or February 1) of each semester in order to receive salary commencing
from August 1 (or February 1). Those who complete the procedures after the
aforementioned date shall receive salary commencing from the actual date of
check-in. For service periods of less than one full month, salary shall be
calculated based on the actual number of days in service. The daily salary
amount shall be calculated by dividing the full monthly salary by the total
number of days in that month.
2. Principles for Salary Advancement Based on Prior Service
For newly appointed faculty members of the University, salary advancement based
on prior service shall be processed in accordance with Teacher Remuneration Act,
the Regulations Governing the Recognition of Pre-Employment Seniority for Salary
Advancement of Teachers, and relevant official interpretations. The principles are
as follows:
(1) Full-time faculty members transferring from public universities: salary shall be
determined by recognizing the originally determined salary grade and level.
(2) Individuals who have previously served as civil servants or faculty members at
private universities: prior service years of equivalent rank and with excellent
service performance may be recognized on an annual basis for salary
advancement, up to the maximum seniority salary for the appointed rank.
(3) Individuals who have previously served in private institution: where the nature of
the previous position is similar to the intended teaching discipline and the work
experience is genuinely required for teaching; where the previous position was
9

full-time and equivalent to the intended faculty rank; and where the service
performance was excellent, prior service years may be conditionally recognized
in accordance with prescribed procedures.
(4) For the prior service recognition methods described in the preceding two
subparagraphs, any number of months less than one year shall not be counted.
D. Seniority-Based Salary Advancement
Faculty members and research personnel who have completed one academic year of
service shall be evaluated by the University based on their teaching, research, and
service performance for the academic year. Based on the evaluation results, base salary
(seniority salary) may be advanced by one grade, up to the maximum seniority salary for
the appointed rank.
Source of Information : Teacher Remuneration Act; Regulations Governing the
Recognition of Pre-Employment Seniority for Salary Advancement of Teachers; Position
Rank Table for Faculty Members and Teaching Assistants of Public Schools; NCCU
Guidelines for Seniority-Based Salary Raises for Faculty Members (promulgated and
implemented on 2021/11/22).
Contact Persons : Personnel Office First Section, extension 62062;
Personnel Office Third Section, extension 63512.
E. Additional Academic Allowances
1. Eligible Applicants : Newly appointed full-time faculty members of the University
(full-time technical experts and research fellows shall apply mutatis mutandis).
2. Application Procedures : After completing the check-in procedures, newly
appointed faculty members shall complete the application form and submit it to
their department or institute for processing in accordance with prescribed
procedures.
3. Standards for Additional Allowances (The monetary value per allowance point
shall be announced separately; currently, one (1) point represents NT$10,000.)
(1) Newly appointed Assistant Professors
10

a. One (1) base subsidy point per month
b. An additional 0.8 subsidy points per month if they serve as a paid principal
investigator for an ongoing National Science and Technology Council (NSTC)
research project at the time of reporting for duty
c. An additional 1.2 subsidy points per month if they are the winner of a major
domestic or international award (such as the Academia Sinica Early-Career
Investigator Research Achievement Award, NSTC Ta-You Wu Memorial Award,
or a comparable domestic/international award)
(2) Newly appointed Associate Professors and Professors
a. An additional 1.5 subsidy points per month if they serve as a paid principal
investigator for an ongoing NSTC research project as a quota-based faculty
member or research fellow at a domestic university or research institute; or if
they have previously worked at a prestigious university or research institute
overseas before reporting for duty at the University
b. An additional 1.5 subsidy points per month if they are the winner of a major
domestic or international award (such as the NSTC Ta-You Wu Memorial Award
or a comparable domestic/international award)
4. Duration of Allowance Payment :
(1) The additional subsidies shall be paid to eligible faculty members on a monthly
basis, up until the end of their first two years at the University. The two-year limit
shall apply regardless of whether subsidy payment is suspended or terminated.
(2) Newly appointed assistant professors who become a paid principal investigator
for a new NSTC research project, who publish two or more research papers in
prestigious journals, or who have other comparable accomplishments within two
years of reporting for duty may apply to extend the subsidy period for another
two years.
5. Restrictions on Allowance Receipt
Newly appointed assistant and associate professors qualifying for the subsidies may
not take on part-time work or teaching engagements off campus during the subsidy
period, barring extraordinary circumstances where express approval is granted by the
University.
11

Source of Information : National Chengchi University Directives Governing the Approval
of Additional Academic Subsidies for Newly Appointed Faculty Members
Contact Person : Personnel Office Third Section, extension 63512.

IV. Promotion (Including Time-Limited Promotion)
A. Promotion
In order to ensure that the University’s appointment and promotion system conforms to
the professional characteristics of each college, the legal system, and the principles of
fairness, justice, and objectivity, the key provisions regarding faculty promotion at the
University are excerpted as follows:
1. Where a faculty member applies for promotion, he/she shall meet the following
conditions:
(1) Years of service required for promotion:
a. In principle, the years of service required for promotion shall be based on
years of teaching at the University. Years of teaching at other domestic
universities, years of teaching at overseas schools recognized by the Ministry
of Education, or years of employment at other academic research institutions
may be counted upon recommendation by the department-level Faculty
Evaluation Committee and approval by the college-level Faculty Evaluation
Committee and the University Faculty Evaluation Committee; however, the
years of teaching at the University must be at least one (1) year.
b. An applicant for promotion to assistant professor shall have served as a
lecturer for three (3) years or more; an applicant for promotion to associate
professor shall have served as an assistant professor for three (3) years or
more; and an applicant for promotion to professor shall have served as an
associate professor for three (3) years or more.
(2) During the period of holding the current position, the faculty member shall have
excellent performance in research, teaching, and service, and shall meet the
review standards of the department (institute, degree program, office, or center)
and the college.
2. Where a faculty member falls under any of the following circumstances, he/she
shall not apply for promotion:
(1) Holding an administrative position in the capacity of a faculty member without
teaching.
13

(2) The actual teaching years have not reached the required years.
(3) After promotion, there are no appropriate courses available to be offered.
(4) After promotion, the teaching hours are insufficient.
(5) The faculty performance evaluation has not been passed.
(6) In the semester of applying for promotion, the faculty member is not actually on
campus to teach courses.
(7) Leave without pay.
(8) Where any of the circumstances under Article 14, Paragraph 1, Article 15,
Paragraph 1, or Article 16, Paragraph 1 of the Teachers’ Act applies, and the case
is still under investigation or in the procedures for dismissal or non-renewal of
appointment; however, where Article 16, Paragraph 1 of the Teachers’ Act
applies due to the faculty member’s failure to meet the University’s promotion
time limit requirements, this shall not be subject to this restriction.
(9) Where any of the circumstances under Article 18, Paragraph 1, Article 21, or
Article 22, Paragraph 1 or Paragraph 2 of the Teachers’ Act applies, and the case
is still under investigation, in the procedures for suspension of appointment, or
during the period of suspension of appointment.
(10) Where any of the circumstances under Article 27, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph
2 or Subparagraph 3 of the Teachers’ Act applies, and the case is still under
investigation or in the procedures for severance.
3. Promotions are processed twice each year:
(1) Faculty promotions at the University are processed twice each year, once in each
semester. The effective dates of promotion are August 1 and February 1,
respectively. Faculty members applying for promotion shall prepare the
promotion materials and submit the application to their affiliated department
(institute, degree program, office, or center) by March 15 of each year (for
promotion effective on August 1 of the same year), or by September 15 of each
year (for promotion effective on February 1 of the following year). Applications
with incomplete materials or submitted after the deadline shall not be accepted.
14

(2) The University Faculty Evaluation Committee adopts a centralized review for
faculty promotion cases. The schedule for review of promotion cases is as
follows:
4. Review items and standards for promotion are as follows:
(1) Review items: research, teaching, and service.
(2) Review standards:
a. The research item shall account for at least 40%; the teaching item may
account for 30% to 50%; and the service item may account for 10% to 30%.
b. Faculty members may choose the allocation of the proportions of each item
by themselves.
c. Departments (institutes, degree programs, offices, and centers) and colleges
shall establish the sufficiency requirements and passing standards for the two
review items of teaching and service. Only where teaching and service meet
the standards set by the departments (institutes, degree programs, offices,
and centers) and colleges, and where the research review score meets the
standard under Article 15, Subparagraph 3 of the University’s Regulations for
Faculty Appointment and Promotion Reviews, may the case be submitted to
the committee meeting for review.
d. Promotion scores shall be calculated by combining the scores for research,
teaching, and service. Only where the total score meets the standards set by

5. In addition to submitting specialized academic works for review, faculty members

6. Format of the review opinion form:

or above (top 10%); Level B: 80–89 points (top 11%–20%); Level C: 75–79 points
(top 21%–25%); Level D: below 75 points (below the top 25%).
(2) Review items: quality, originality, and contribution of the applicant’s
representative works (30%); quality of research achievements and professional
performance compared with faculty members of the same field and rank (30%);
quantity of research achievements and professional performance compared with
16

faculty members of the same field and rank (30%); future development potential
in the applicant’s professional field and related academic performance (10%).

meeting : At least five (5) reviewers shall be sent for review. The thresholds for
submission to the Faculty Evaluation Committee meeting are as follows:
(1) For promotion to professor, the overall ratings shall reach at least four (4)
reviewers rating Level C (75 points) or above, including three (3) reviewers rating
Level B (80 points) or above.
(2) For promotion to associate professor, the overall ratings shall reach at least four
(4) reviewers rating Level C (75 points) or above, including two (2) reviewers
rating Level B (80 points) or above.
(3) Where the number of external reviewers exceeds five (5), the threshold for
submission to the committee meeting shall be calculated proportionally and shall
not be lower than the above proportions.
8. Promotion of professional technical personnel : Promotion of full-time
professional technical personnel shall be processed mutatis mutandis in
accordance with the relevant provisions for faculty promotion of the University.
However, concrete deeds, special attainments, or achievements may be submitted
in lieu of specialized academic works for review.
9. Where the operating guidelines for appointment and promotion of any college
and any department (institute, degree program, office, or center) are stricter than
the University’s Regulations for Faculty Appointment and Promotion Reviews such
guidelines shall prevail.

B. Governing the Promotion Schedule of New Faculty
In order to encourage newly appointed faculty members to improve the standards of
teaching, research, and service, the University has specially formulated the University’s
Regulations Governing the Promotion Schedule of New Faculty, which have been
implemented since Academic Year 2002. The key provisions are excerpted as follows. In
addition, Article 6 of the University’s full-time faculty employment contract provides
that newly appointed faculty members of ranks below associate professor are subject to
the University’s Regulations Governing the Promotion Schedule of New Faculty:
1. Eligible applicants and time limits for promotion:
(1) Full-time assistant professors and lecturers initially appointed by the University
shall pass promotion within six (6) years after the initial appointment; full-time
associate professors initially appointed by the University shall pass promotion
within eight (8) years after the initial appointment.
(2) Full-time professional technical personnel of the University and newly appointed
lecturers whose teaching content is mainly foreign language training may, upon
application submitted by the appointing unit, be exempted from the restrictions
of these Regulations. After approval by the President, they shall instead be
subject to the University’s Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations.
(3) Full-time associate research fellows, assistant research fellows, and research
assistants initially appointed by the University on and after August 1, 2009 shall
apply these Regulations by analogy.
2. Extension of the time limit for promotion : Due to childbirth, parental leave
without pay, suffering from major illness, or other major reasons, a faculty
member may submit supporting documents and apply for a resolution by the
Faculty Evaluation Committees at all levels to extend the time limit for promotion
by two (2) years. Where an extension of the time limit for promotion is applied for
due to major illness or other major reasons, the same reason shall be limited to
one (1) application.
3. Teaching restrictions: The annual teaching hours of newly appointed faculty
members shall not be higher than twelve (12) hours; the number of courses for
preparation shall not exceed four (4) courses; excess teaching hour fees shall not
18

be received; and, except as specially approved, newly appointed faculty members
shall not concurrently hold other employment or engage in concurrent teaching
within or outside the University.
4. Time-limited promotion report:
(1) Each academic year, newly appointed faculty members shall provide a written
explanation of progress in teaching, research, and service. The head of the
department (institute) shall provide written recommendations regarding the
explanation in order to assist the faculty member in completing promotion on
schedule, and the matter shall be reported to the department (institute) and
college Faculty Evaluation Committees.
(2) The University’s “Time-Limited Promotion Report Form for Newly Appointed
Faculty (Research Personnel)” is divided into two forms: “within four (4) years
after arrival” and “from the fifth (5th) year after arrival,” as follows:
a. Within four (4) years after arrival: newly appointed faculty and research
personnel shall check the progress items for teaching, research, and service,
and state reflections or opinions (if any; if none, no need to fill in), and report
to the department (institute) and college Faculty Evaluation Committees. After
approval by the college-level Faculty Evaluation Committee, the department
(institute) shall provide copies to the newly appointed faculty and research
personnel and the college for reference.
b. From the fifth (5th) year after arrival: newly appointed faculty and research
personnel shall provide a comprehensive narrative on the progress of
teaching, research, and service, including difficulties encountered and
assistance needed. After reporting to the department (institute) and college
Faculty Evaluation Committees, the matter shall be further submitted to the
University for approval. After approval, the department (institute) shall
provide copies to the newly appointed faculty and research personnel, the
college, and the Personnel Office.
5. Failure to pass promotion within the prescribed time limit :
Where faculty members of any rank fail to pass promotion within the prescribed
time limit, salary advancement shall not be granted; they shall not concurrently
19

hold employment or engage in concurrent teaching within or outside the
University; they shall not serve as members of Faculty Evaluation Committees at
all levels; they shall not apply for secondment or for overseas research, teaching,
or advanced study; and the years of service for senior outstanding faculty shall be
recalculated, and only after achieving excellent performance for ten (10)
consecutive years and meeting the service milestones of ten (10), twenty (20),
thirty (30), and forty (40) years may they apply for the senior outstanding faculty
awards.
Where assistant professors and lecturers remain unpromoted by the eighth (8th)
year, or associate professors remain unpromoted by the tenth (10th) year, in
addition to those who meet retirement eligibility and may apply for retirement,
their appointments shall not be renewed after (i) a resolution adopted by at least
two-thirds (2/3) of the attending members, with at least two-thirds (2/3) of the
attending members voting in favor, at the Faculty Evaluation Committee, and (ii)
approval by the competent educational administrative authority.

V. Performance Evaluation
A. Basic Provisions
1. Work Summary Form: Each year, faculty members of the University update a work
summary form for the preceding year in the aspects of teaching, research, and
service. The head of the department (institute) and the Dean may provide
suggestions regarding its contents.
2. Performance Evaluation: The faculty performance evaluation of the University
evaluates overall performance over a five (5)-year period (including teaching,
research, and service), and shall be conducted in accordance with the University’s
Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations. The key provisions are excerpted as
follows:
(1) After a faculty member’s service reaches each five (5)-year period, the faculty
member shall undergo evaluation in the first semester of the sixth (6th) year.
(2) Where a faculty member has given birth, is on parental leave without pay, suffers
from a major illness, or has other major reasons, he/she may submit supporting
documents and, upon resolution by the Faculty Evaluation Committees at all
levels, apply for a deferral of the evaluation, with a maximum of two (2) years for
each deferral. For those applying for deferral of evaluation, except for childbirth,
parental leave without pay, and major illness, the same reason shall be limited to
one (1) application.
(3) Faculty members who do not pass their evaluation, within the period for re-
evaluation, receive guidance from the faculty member’s affiliated unit or the
Faculty Development Center and submit an improvement plan, which shall be
submitted to the college and University Faculty Evaluation Committees for
record. The faculty member shall pass the re-evaluation within three (3) years.
The semester in which the faculty member is required to undergo evaluation
shall not be postponed due to the re-evaluation.
(4) Full-time associate professors, assistant professors, and lecturers who are initially
appointed and have not yet been promoted shall be handled in accordance with
the University’s Regulations Governing the Promotion Schedule of New Faculty.
Those who successfully gained promotion after arrival in their NCCU faculty
21

member position shall be considered to have passed their first evaluation. For
those who pass the University’s time-limited promotion, starting from the
semester in which the promotion takes effect, they shall undergo an overall
evaluation once every five (5) years. For other faculty members, those who pass
promotion may be deemed to have passed one (1) evaluation. A recently
promoted faculty member who waives their evaluation due to their promotion
will have their next evaluation date scheduled five (5) years after the semester
in which their promotion takes effect.
(5) Faculty members who fail the overall evaluation are ineligible for salary increase
starting from the subsequent academic year; starting from the subsequent
semester, they may not apply for promotion, receive additional payment for extra
hours, holding off-campus part-time jobs/teaching positions, serving as members
of any level of faculty evaluation committees, applying for temporary
transfer applying for research leave, or applying for paid overseas teaching,
research, or further education. They shall not be selected as outstanding
teaching faculty of the University, faculty members and research personnel with
distinguished service, or recipients of the Confucius Distinguished Teaching Award;
and the years of service for senior outstanding faculty shall be recalculated to
reach ten (10) consecutive years of excellent performance, and only upon meeting
service milestones of ten (10), twenty (20), thirty (30), and forty (40) years may
they apply for senior outstanding faculty awards.
(6) Teachers who are required to undergo evaluation and either fail to pass or do not
submit a re-evaluation by the due date, unless eligible for retirement and applying
accordingly, shall not be reappointed. This decision is subject to the approval of
the Teacher Review Committee, with at least two-thirds of the members in
attendance and a two-thirds majority vote of the attending members. The final
decision requires approval from the supervisory educational administration
authority.
(7) Full-time researchers and full-time professional technical staff of NCCU, may be
separately prescribed by the appointing unit by reference to this Regulations.

VI. External Employment and Concurrent Teaching
A. External Employment
1. External employment shall be handled in accordance with the Ministry of
Education Principles Governing External Employment of Full-Time Teachers at
Public Schools at All Levels, the Ministry of Education Regulations Governing
External Employment of Teachers Holding Concurrent Administrative Positions at
National Schools at All Levels, and the University’s Regulations Governing External
Employment of Full-Time Faculty Members.
2. Pursuant to the University’s Regulations Governing External Employment of Full-
Time Faculty Members, faculty members’ external employment shall not affect
their primary duties and shall comply with the University’s minimum teaching load
and work requirements. Except for cases where external employment occurs
automatically due to changes in position or is mandated by relevant laws and
regulations, faculty members shall submit an application in advance and may
engage in external employment only after obtaining written approval from the
University. For continued external employment upon expiration or changes in
external employment positions, a new application shall be submitted.
In addition, where external employment requires preliminary nomination or
election procedures by a for-profit enterprise, institution, or organization, faculty
members shall report in writing to the University for approval at the time they are
invited to accept nomination or election to such positions. Where faculty
members engage in external employment with non-profit enterprises, institutions,
or organizations, they may apply by reference to the aforementioned provisions.
Where faculty members are not elected to such positions, they shall notify the
University.
3. Faculty members applying for external employment with for-profit enterprises,
institutions, or organizations shall be evaluated by the department (institute or
center) as meeting the required standards, and shall be approved by the
departmental (institute or center) affairs meeting or relevant meeting. The starting
date of the external employment permission shall be the date stated in the
University’s written approval letter.
24

Where the period of external employment reaches six (6) months or longer, the
University and the for-profit enterprise shall enter into a cooperation agreement
from the above permission date, stipulating the collection of academic feedback
fees. The academic feedback fee shall not be less than the total amount of one (1)
month of the faculty member’s salary received from the University per year, and
shall not be less than ten percent (10%) of the external employment income.
Where the external employment remuneration exceeds the faculty member’s total
salary, other feedback mechanisms shall be separately agreed upon with the
University in order to implement industry–academia cooperation.
For faculty members whose monthly external employment remuneration exceeds
their total salary, each department (institute or center) shall submit for
confirmation by the departmental (institute or center) affairs meeting or the
Faculty Evaluation Committee an analysis report on the impact on the faculty
member’s primary duties, an evaluation of the substantive benefits of the external
employment to industry–academia cooperation, the reasonableness of the
academic feedback fee amount, and the results of periodic evaluations.
Where faculty members serve as independent directors of listed (or over-the-
counter) companies, or unlisted public companies that have been approved by the
board of directors or shareholders’ meeting to apply for listing (or OTC trading),
the amount of the academic feedback fee shall comply with the University’s
standards based on company capitalization.
4. Faculty members who do not concurrently hold administrative positions shall, in
principle, engage in external employment with no more than three (3) for-profit
enterprises, institutions, or organizations. Faculty members who concurrently hold
administrative positions shall, in principle, engage in external employment with no
more than two (2) such entities; however, serving as an independent director shall
be limited to one (1) position. Where the concurrently held positions primarily
involve regular business operations, the total external employment hours shall not
exceed eight (8) hours per week.
5. External employment remuneration (including transportation fees, attendance
fees, etc.) shall, in principle, be transferred and disbursed by the University, and
25

shall not be paid directly by the employing institution or organization. However,
this restriction shall not apply where payment is made through electronic funds
transfer and the employing institution or organization notifies this University by
official written correspondence after payment has been made.
6. Where faculty members engage in external employment without complying with
the relevant regulations, the University shall terminate such external employment
and submit the case to the Faculty Evaluation Committees at all levels for review.
Any external employment remuneration received during the period of violation
shall be recovered.
7. Other regulations of the University related to external employment include the
following:
(1) Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations: faculty members who fail to pass
the evaluation shall not engage in internal or external employment or concurrent
teaching.
(2) Regulations Governing the Promotion Schedule of New Faculty: prior to passing
promotion, newly appointed faculty members shall not engage in internal or
external employment or concurrent teaching, except where specially approved.
(3) Directives Governing the Approval of Additional Academic Subsidies for Newly
Appointed Faculty Members: during the period of receiving such allowances,
newly appointed assistant professors and associate professors shall not engage
in external employment or concurrent teaching (including internal continuing
education and extension education courses), except under special circumstances
approved on a case-by-case basis.
8. External employment cases, in addition to being submitted to the University by
the employing institution or organization through official correspondence, may
also be processed by downloading and completing the Application Form for
Permission for External Employment (separate forms for faculty members with and
without concurrent administrative positions) from the Personnel Office website
under “Forms Download” → “Faculty and Research Personnel” → “Secondment,
External Employment, Substitute Teaching, Teaching Load, and Concurrent
Teaching,” and submitting the application for approval through administrative
26

procedures.

B. Concurrent Teaching Outside the University
Full-time faculty members of the University who engage in concurrent teaching outside
the University shall obtain prior consent from the University, either through prior
consultation by the external teaching institution or by submitting an application form to
the University for approval before engaging in such teaching. At the latest, the internal
approval procedures shall be completed before the start of the semester in which the
concurrent teaching is intended. Where the approval procedures are not completed
before the start of the semester, permission for external concurrent teaching shall not
be granted. A summary of the relevant regulations is as follows:
1. Article 8 of the University’s full-time faculty employment contract: external
concurrent teaching by faculty members shall be handled in accordance with the
regulations of the Ministry of Education and the University, and shall be subject to
University approval. Where approval is granted, the maximum concurrent teaching
time during working hours shall be four (4) hours per week.
2. Article 10 of the University’s Regulations for Faculty Performance Evaluation:
faculty members who fail to pass the overall evaluation shall not engage in internal
or external employment or concurrent teaching starting from the following
semester.
3. Regulations for Time-Limited Promotion of Newly Appointed Faculty Members of
the University:
27

(1) Article 3: prior to passing promotion, newly appointed faculty members shall not
engage in internal or external employment or concurrent teaching, except where
specially approved.
(2) Article 4: faculty members of all ranks who fail to pass promotion within the
prescribed time limits (six (6) years for lecturers and assistant professors; eight
(8) years for associate professors) shall not engage in internal or external
employment or concurrent teaching.
4. Article 4 of the University’s Guidelines for Additional Academic Allowances for
Newly Appointed Faculty Members: during the period of receiving such
allowances, newly appointed assistant professors and associate professors shall
not engage in external employment or concurrent teaching (including internal
continuing education and extension education courses), except under special
circumstances approved on a case-by-case basis.
5. Regulations Governing Faculty Teaching Load and the Calculation of Excess
Teaching Hour Fees of the University :
(1) Article 3: the minimum teaching load for full-time faculty members is twelve (12)
hours per academic year. Where any college, department, or institute stipulates
a higher requirement, such stipulations shall prevail. The annual teaching load
for faculty members holding concurrent administrative positions shall be subject
to Article 4 of the same Regulations.
(2) Article 8: the total weekly teaching hours undertaken by full-time faculty
members outside the regular academic system shall not exceed those
undertaken within the regular academic system.
(3) Article 11: only where a full-time faculty member teaches more than sixteen (16)
hours within the University’s regular academic system and has obtained prior
approval may he/she engage in external concurrent teaching during working
hours, with a maximum of four (4) hours per week. Where the teaching hours
are sixteen (16) hours or fewer, external concurrent teaching during working
hours shall not be permitted. External concurrent teaching outside working
hours shall also require prior approval.
6. Curriculum Streamlining Program of the University:
28

(1) Section 4, Subparagraph (2), Item 1, Subitem (5): only where a full-time faculty
member teaches more than sixteen (16) hours within the University’s regular
academic system and has obtained prior approval may he/she engage in external
concurrent teaching; where the teaching hours are sixteen (16) hours or fewer,
external concurrent teaching during working hours shall not be permitted.
External concurrent teaching outside working hours shall also require prior
approval.
(2) Section 4, Subparagraph (2), Item 1, Subitem (6): full-time faculty members may
engage in concurrent teaching at other universities within the Taiwan University
System on the principle of inter-university reciprocity and shall not be subject to
the restriction in the preceding subitem; however, prior approval is still required,
and the teaching shall be limited to one (1) course per academic year.
7. Other relevant regulations regarding external concurrent teaching are as follows:
(1) Faculty members who receive reduced teaching loads within the University
under the following circumstances are not suitable for engaging in external
concurrent teaching:
a. The purpose of reducing teaching loads for those concurrently holding
administrative (supervisory) positions is to allow them to focus on
administrative duties; therefore, they should not engage in external
concurrent teaching.
b. The purpose of reducing teaching loads for outstanding talents is to allow
them to focus on research or University academic missions; therefore, they
should not engage in external concurrent teaching.
c. Faculty members subject to time-limited promotion requirements, pursuant to
Article 3 of the University’s Regulations for Time-Limited Promotion of Newly
Appointed Faculty Members, shall not engage in internal or external

Furthermore, under current regulations, their annual teaching load shall not

they shall not engage in internal or external concurrent teaching (including
during and outside working hours).

(2) Faculty members and research personnel engaging in external concurrent
teaching shall obtain University approval in accordance with regulations.
Concurrent teaching during working hours shall not exceed four (4) hours per
week, and teaching hours outside the regular academic system shall not exceed

(3) Where faculty members apply for external concurrent teaching in the first

8. Resolutions of the meeting on discussing the teaching hour limits for research

VII. Secondment
A. Basic Provisions (Secondment)
Faculty members at the rank of associate professor or above who have served at the
University for three (3) years or more may be seconded to assume full-time positions in
government agencies, public or private universities and colleges, publicly or privately
operated enterprises and institutions, academic institutions, foundations, incorporated
associations, juridical persons, administrative juridical persons, etc.; however, in special
circumstances approved by the President, this restriction shall not apply.
The position to which a faculty member is seconded shall be related to his/her expertise
or required due to special operational needs, and shall be processed in accordance with
the University’s Guidelines for Handling Faculty Secondment. The key provisions are
excerpted as follows:
1. Term and Number of Secondments :
(1) Each application for secondment shall be for a maximum of four (4) years. Where
the first secondment period is less than four (4) years, an application for
extension of the secondment period shall still be limited to a total of four (4)
years.
(2) For secondment to public or private universities and colleges, the faculty
member must concurrently hold a position at or above the level of a first-tier
supervisor at such institution. For secondment to a public office with a fixed
term, where the term exceeds four (4) years, the secondment period shall be
handled in accordance with the term of office, and shall be limited to one (1)
secondment.
(3) A faculty member may apply for secondment again only after returning to the
University for two (2) years upon completion of the secondment. A second
secondment shall be limited to one (1) time, and the total number of years of
secondment shall not exceed six (6) years.
2. Secondment Procedures : Secondment of faculty members shall be initiated by the
seconding agency (institution) or school through official correspondence to the
University. The department (institute, degree program, office, or center) shall
submit a written evaluation report, which shall be approved by the departmental
31

(institute, degree program, office, or center) affairs meeting or relevant meeting,
and shall then be processed after obtaining the consent of the Dean and the
President.
B. Other Matters Requiring Attention
1. During the secondment period, the faculty member shall apply for leave without
pay.
2. Where a faculty member is seconded to a private university or a publicly or
privately operated enterprise or institution, the seconding school or institution
shall enter into a cooperation agreement with the University, stipulating the
collection of academic feedback fees.
3. During the secondment period, the faculty member shall return to the University
each semester to fulfill an obligation to teach two (2) credits or more; however,
this restriction shall not apply under special circumstances approved on a case-by-
case basis.
4. Whether the years of secondment service may be counted for the purposes of
professors’ sabbatical leave, promotion, seniority-based salary advancement,
retirement, survivor benefits, or severance shall be handled in accordance with
relevant regulations.
5. Return to the University from secondment shall be notified to the University by
the seconding agency (institution) or school through official correspondence, or
the faculty member may apply through administrative procedures. The faculty
member shall resume duties from the day following the expiration of the
secondment period. Where the faculty member fails to resume duties after the
deadline, except for reasons not attributable to the faculty member, it shall be
deemed as resignation.
6. Secondment of research personnel shall be handled by reference to the
University’s Guidelines for Handling Faculty Secondment.
7. Where any department, institute, or college has stricter regulations regarding
secondment procedures or the secondment period, such regulations shall prevail.

VIII. Teaching and Service Awards
A. Distinguished Service Award for Faculty and Researchers
1. Selection Provisions: In order to commend faculty members and research
personnel who have made concrete contributions to the development and
promotion of University affairs, the University has formulated the Regulations
Governing Distinguished Service Award for Faculty and Researchers. Each academic
year, distinguished service faculty members and research personnel shall be
selected. Those who have cumulatively received the distinguished service award
three (3) times shall be selected as exceptionally distinguished faculty and research
personnel.
2. Award Amounts: Recipients of the distinguished service award shall be publicly
commended by the University and shall receive an award of NT$60,000 and a
plaque. Exceptionally distinguished faculty and research personnel shall
additionally receive an exceptional award of NT$20,000.
3. Eligibility:
(1) Full-time faculty members and research personnel who have served at the
University for three (3) years or more and have excellent service achievements
may be recommended as candidates for the distinguished service award.
(2) Those who have had any of the following circumstances within the most recent
three (3) years shall not be selected as distinguished service faculty members or
research personnel:
a. Those who have not passed the University’s faculty performance evaluation
and whose cases have been recorded by the University Faculty Evaluation
Committee.
b. Those with poor moral character, conduct, or professional ethics, as verified to
be true.
4. Quota: In principle, the number of recipients of the distinguished service award
shall be one percent (1%) of the total number of full-time faculty members and
research personnel for the academic year of selection.
5. Selection Procedures and Standards
34

(1) The selection process shall be conducted once each academic year. Candidates
shall be nominated by the Deans of colleges or heads of first-tier administrative
units (including centers). Where Deans of colleges and heads of first-tier
administrative units (including centers) meet the criteria for excellent service

(2) For those participating in the selection for the first time, all service achievements

However, for those who have previously received the award and participate in

B. Awards for Senior Outstanding Faculty
1. For full-time qualified faculty members currently employed (excluding
research personnel), those who, as of the end of July each year, have
continuously actually engaged in teaching work for ten (10), twenty (20), thirty
(30), or forty (40) years with excellent performance shall receive award funds
allocated by the Ministry of Education, and shall be publicly commended by
the University on Teachers’ Day.
2. “Excellent performance” means that, in accordance with university self-
established evaluation regulations [the University’s Regulations for Faculty
Performance Evaluation and the University’s Regulations for Time-Limited
Promotion of Newly Appointed Faculty Members] or self-established criteria for
recognizing excellent performance based on academic-year evaluations, the
evaluation or assessment results for the most recent ten (10) years have all been
approved, advanced, or granted awards, and that the faculty member has not
been subject to criminal or disciplinary penalties or demerit-level penalties or
above in routine assessments. Where the evaluation or assessment results for the

most recent ten (10) years do not reach excellent performance, except in cases of
major illness with sick leave exceeding regulations or cases where the faculty
member did not come to the University to provide service for the entire year due

shall be recalculated, and only upon meeting service milestones of ten (10),
twenty (20), thirty (30), or forty (40) years may the faculty member apply for the

IX. Faculty Code of Ethics (Including Regulations Governing the Review of
Academic Ethics Cases)
A. Faculty Code of Ethics
1. The University’s Faculty Code of Ethics was reviewed and approved by the 152nd
consecutive University Affairs Meeting on March 2, 2009, and the 153rd University
Affairs Meeting on April 25, 2009, and was promulgated and implemented on May
21, 2009, with the expectation that, through the formulation of this Code, the self-
discipline of the University’s faculty members will be strengthened and the
expectations of the academic community will be met.
2. This Code first sets forth the basic philosophy of faculty members in Chapter 1,
and then provides regulations respectively regarding teaching ethics, academic
ethics, service ethics, and interpersonal ethics, for a total of five (5) chapters.
3. Article 3 of the University’s full-time faculty employment contract provides that
faculty members of the University bear obligations including teaching, research,
service, counseling, serving as class advisors, and attending relevant meetings, and
shall strictly comply with the University’s Faculty Code of Ethics. Chapter 5 of the
above Code on interpersonal ethics further provides that faculty members shall
not engage in acts or speech of sexual assault or sexual harassment toward
colleagues or students.
Source of Information : Faculty Code of Ethics of the University.
Contact Person : Personnel Office Second Section, extension 63312.
B. Academic Ethics Cases
In order to handle matters involving violations of academic ethics by the University’s
faculty members and research personnel and violations of the regulations governing the
qualifications of faculty members submitted for review, the University, in accordance
with the Regulations Governing Accreditation of Teacher Qualifications at Junior
Colleges and Institutions of Higher Education, the Principles for Handling Violations of
Regulations Governing the Qualifications of Teachers Submitted for Review at
37

Institutions of Higher Education, the Principles for Handling Academic Ethics Cases at
Institutions of Higher Education, and the Key Points for the Handling and Review of
Academic Ethics Cases of the National Science and Technology Council, has formulated
the University’s Regulations Governing the Review of Academic Ethics Cases of Faculty
Members and Research Personnel. The key provisions are excerpted as follows:
1. The University has established an Academic Ethics Committee, which is
responsible for accepting, investigating, and reviewing cases involving violations of
academic ethics and violations of the regulations governing the qualifications of
teachers submitted for review.
2. “Violations of academic ethics” and “violations of the regulations governing the
qualifications of teachers submitted for review” refer to any of the following
circumstances involving a faculty member or research personnel of the University:
(1) Fabrication: forging or fabricating non-existent application materials, research
data, processes, or results.
(2) Falsification: unauthorized alteration of application materials, research data,
processes, or results.
(3) Plagiarism: using another person’s application materials, research data, works, or
results without indicating the source. Where the source is improperly indicated
and the circumstances are serious, it shall be deemed plagiarism.
(4) Fraud: obtaining or presenting research data or results through deception,
misrepresentation, or other improper means.
(5) Ghostwriting: a paper or work is written by a person other than the author; or a
project application or research results report is written by a person unrelated to
the project.
(6) Duplicate publication without disclosure: publishing the same academic results
or an important part thereof in different journals or books without disclosure.
(7) Failure to indicate that part of the content has been previously published as
results or works: using content, paragraphs, or research results from one’s own
previously published works without disclosure.
38

(8) Improper citation: referencing another person’s research data or results without
proper citation in accordance with academic norms or customary practice, where
the uncited portion is not the core of the work or is insufficient to mislead as to
its originality.
(9) False entries in the curriculum vitae for teacher qualification review (referring to
the parts involving review matters, excluding obvious errors such as mistaken
entry of identity information or other similar apparent errors), false entries in co-
author certification, failure to truthfully indicate a representative work as co-
authored and submit co-author certification.
(10) Forging or falsifying academic degree certificates, employment experience
certificates, proof of achievements, proof that specialized academic works have
been accepted by publications, or co-author certifications.
(11) Where the applicant, or through another person, engages in solicitation,
lobbying, inducement, threats, or other interference with reviewers or the
review process, or where the applicant influences paper reviews by illegal or
improper means.
(12) Other conduct in violation of academic ethics.
3. For academic ethics cases determined to be established upon review by the
Academic Ethics Committee, depending on the severity of the case, the
Committee may recommend one (1) or more of the following disciplinary actions
and submit such recommendations to the University Faculty Evaluation
Committee for review:
(1) For a certain period, no salary advancement shall be granted, and applications
for promotion, secondment, internal or external employment or concurrent
teaching, applications for various research projects, awards, and subsidies shall
not be permitted.
(2) For a certain period, applications for professors’ sabbatical leave for research,
extension of service, serving as members of Faculty Evaluation Committees at all
levels within the University, or serving in academic administrative supervisory
positions shall not be permitted.
39

(3) Recovery of research awards and subsidy funds related to the case, suspension
of payments other than statutory salary, or recovery of statutory salary in
accordance with law.
(4) In accordance with the procedures prescribed by the Teachers’ Act and the
University’s regulations, and upon approval by the Ministry of Education,
dismissal, suspension of appointment, or non-renewal of appointment.
(5) For academic ethics cases involving regulations governing teacher qualification
submission for review, in accordance with the Regulations Governing
Accreditation of Teacher Qualifications at Junior Colleges and Institutions of
Higher Education and the Principles for Handling Violations of Regulations
Governing the Qualifications of Teachers Submitted for Review at Institutions of
Higher Education, etc., failure to pass the qualification determination, refusal to
accept applications for teacher qualification determination for a certain period,
reporting to the Ministry of Education for revocation of teacher qualifications
from the relevant rank onward, and recovery of the teacher certificate.
(6) For academic ethics cases not involving violations of regulations governing
teacher qualification submission for review, written warnings, participation in
academic ethics-related courses for a certain period and obtaining proof thereof,
etc., may additionally be imposed in accordance with the Principles for Handling
Academic Ethics Cases at Institutions of Higher Education.

XI. Sabbatical Leaves of Professors and Associate Professors
A. Seniority Requirements and Sabbatical Period
Professors, research fellows, and Professor-level Technical Expert who have completed
seven (7) semesters or seven (7) academic years of service, and who have served at the
University for at least three (3) years, may, upon passing the University’s review, apply
for sabbatical leave to engage in academic research work approved by the University.
Where the service seniority reaches seven (7) semesters or more, sabbatical leave for
one (1) semester may be granted; where the service seniority reaches seven (7)
academic years or more, sabbatical leave for one (1) academic year may be granted.
Full-time associate professors, associate research fellows, and associate Professor-level
Technical Expert who have continuously served at the University for seven (7) semesters
or more may apply for sabbatical leave for one (1) semester, limited to one (1) time. In
addition, the sabbatical research must be related to the specialized academic works
submitted for promotion.
The sabbatical period shall be consistent with the semester in order to facilitate course
arrangements.
B. Rules for Deduction of Sabbatical Seniority
Within the seven (7) semesters or seven (7) academic years prior to applying for
sabbatical leave, where a faculty member has been approved by the University to
engage in domestic or overseas-further studies, overseas lecturing, inspection visits,
teaching, or research for a period of six (6) months or more, or where the faculty
member has been on leave without pay or during the period of suspension of
appointment, such seniority shall be deducted; seniority before and after may be
combined for calculation.
For service seniority as a professor at other domestic or overseas universities that has
not been previously counted for sabbatical leave, a maximum of three and a half (3.5)
years may be counted.
C. Circumstances Where Sabbatical Leave Shall Not Be Granted
49

1. During an approved extended service period after reaching the age of sixty-five
(65).
2. Pursuant to the University’s Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations, where
the overall evaluation of the faculty member has not been recorded and approved
by the University Faculty Evaluation Committee.
3. Where the faculty member has been approved for overseas-lecturing, or domestic
or overseas further studies or research, and has not yet fulfilled the required
service obligation.
4. Where the faculty member has returned from secondment and has not yet
completed one (1) year of service.
5. Number limitation：In principle, the number of faculty members on sabbatical
leave each year in each department (institute) shall not exceed fifteen percent
(15%) of the number of professors in the department (institute) (rounded up to
the nearest whole number). Where the result is less than one (1) person, it may be
counted as one (1) person. In addition, in principle, the total quota for
secondment, sabbatical leave, lecturing, further studies, and research shall be
fifteen percent (15%) of the total number of faculty members in the department
or institute (rounded up to the nearest whole number).
D. Application Time
Each year, the University processes applications for sabbatical leave for the second
semester of the following academic year in April, and processes applications for the
following academic year in October. (Example: applications for the second semester of
Academic Year 2026 are processed in April 2026; applications for Academic Year 2027
are processed in October 2026.) Those intending to take sabbatical leave shall submit
applications within the prescribed time limits and shall commence sabbatical leave in
the semester following the completion of the required service seniority.
E. Reminders
1. During the sabbatical period：
50

In principle, the sabbatical period shall be for engaging in academic research. The
faculty member shall not hold other full-time paid positions, nor concurrently hold
academic or administrative supervisory positions at the University; as a rule,
he/she shall also not concurrently serve as the head of a non-established unit.
However, concurrently serving as the head of a research project, upon approval, is
not subject to this restriction. Where the faculty member engages in academic
research work other than that approved, he/she shall report it to the department
(institute) Faculty Evaluation Committee for record.
2. Upon completion of the sabbatical period :
The faculty member shall return to the University to resume service immediately,
and within three (3) months after returning, shall submit a written report on the
academic research undertaken. After the report is reviewed and approved by the
department (institute) Faculty Evaluation Committee, the report shall be
submitted through administrative procedures for the President’s approval, and
shall be uploaded to the University’s Academic Achievements Database. Where
the report is not submitted by the deadline, sabbatical seniority for the overdue
period shall be deducted on a monthly basis.
Source of Information : Regulations Governing the Sabbatical Leaves of Professors and
Associate Professors.

XII. Overseas Lecturing, Research, and Further Studies
A. Seniority Requirements
Faculty members and research personnel within the established staffing system who
apply to engage in overseas lecturing, research, or further studies shall have served in a
full-time position at the University for three (3) years or more. Applicants shall submit
documents including a teaching plan, a research or advanced study plan that meets
teaching needs, and letters of consent from overseas academic, research, or other
relevant institutions. After review and approval by the department (institute) Faculty
Evaluation Committee, the application shall be submitted for approval by the President.
B. Quota Limitations
The number of faculty members from each department (institute) engaging in overseas
lecturing, research, or further studies in any given year shall not exceed ten percent
(10%) of the total number of full-time faculty members in that department (institute) at
the same time (rounded up to the nearest whole number). The total number approved
University-wide shall not exceed five percent (5%) of the total number of full-time
faculty members (rounded up to the nearest whole number). In principle, the total
quota for faculty secondment, sabbatical leave, lecturing, further studies, and research
shall be fifteen percent (15%) of the total number of faculty members in the department
(institute) (rounded up to the nearest whole number).
C. Categories of Application
Applications by faculty members for overseas lecturing, research, or further studies are
classified into two categories: “University-Nominated” and “Self-Applied.”
For those who are University-nominated, leave with pay shall be granted; for those who
apply on their own initiative, leave without pay shall be granted. In all cases, the period
shall be limited to one (1) year.
In addition, applications for overseas lecturing, research, or further studies shall, in
principle, align with the academic semester. Where the period is less than three (3)
52

months, it shall be conducted during winter or summer vacation in order to safeguard
students’ right to education.
D. Application Procedures
1. For candidates nominated by departments (institutes) based on development
needs or for purposes of academic exchange, the application shall be reviewed
and approved by the University review committee and then submitted to the
President for final approval.
2. For applications for overseas activities subsidized by the National Science and
Technology Council or other government agencies or academic research
institutions, the review procedures shall be handled in accordance with the
relevant regulations of the funding authority.
3. Personnel who apply on their own initiative for overseas lecturing, research, or
further studies shall submit the application for review and approval by the
department (institute) Faculty Evaluation Committee at least two (2) months prior
to departure, and then submit it to the President for approval.
E. Circumstances Where Overseas Lecturing, Research, or Further
Studies Shall Not Be Permitted
1. Where a faculty member has been approved for overseas lecturing, research, or
further studies and has not yet completed the required service obligation.
2. Where a professor has returned from sabbatical leave and has not yet completed
one (1) year of service at the University.
3. During an approved extended service period after reaching the age of sixty-five
(65).
4. Pursuant to the University’s Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations, where
the overall evaluation of the faculty member has not been recorded and approved
by the University Faculty Evaluation Committee.
5. Where a faculty member has returned from secondment and has not yet
completed one (1) year of service; however, this restriction shall not apply to
53

secondments approved prior to the promulgation and implementation of the
amended provisions at the 169th University Affairs Meeting on June 29, 2012.
6. Where service obligations are required under other applicable laws or regulations.
F. Service Obligations and Submission of Reports
1. For those granted leave with pay, the service obligation upon returning to the
University shall be twice the duration of the leave-with-pay period. For those
granted leave without pay, the service obligation upon returning shall be equal to
the duration of the leave-without-pay period.
2. Within three (3) months after returning to the University upon completion of the
overseas activity, the faculty member shall submit a lecturing, research, or further
studies report to the Office of Research and Development and the affiliated
department (institute).
Source of Information : Regulations Governing Faculty Members’ Overseas Lecturing,
Research, and Advanced Studies; Operating Guidelines for Reviewing Department

Research, and Further Studies.

XV. Retirement and Survivor Benefits
A. Retirement
1. Applicable Persons
(1) Defined-Benefit Retirement and Survivor Benefits System: Current faculty and
staff of National Chengchi University or other public schools, or faculty and staff
who separated from service on or before June 30, 2023, as well as those who
first assumed a faculty/staff position on or after July 1, 2023 but have years of
service that are applicable to the existing defined-benefit system.
(2) Individual Retirement Account Retirement and Survivor Benefits System: Faculty
and staff who, on or after July 1, 2023, first assume employment at public
schools and are appointed or selected in accordance with statutory
qualifications.
a. Individual retirement account: Public service personnel who first assume
service on or after July 1, 2023 are subject to the “defined-contribution”
retirement and survivor benefits system, under which monthly contributions
made jointly by the public service personnel and the government, as well as
any voluntary additional contributions by the public service personnel, are
deposited into an individual retirement account as reserves for the payment
of retirement and survivor benefits.
b. Additional contributions:
(a) Compound interest effect of accumulated savings: Public service
personnel may voluntarily make additional contributions, up to a
maximum of 5.25% of twice the amount of their seniority-based salary.
That is, in addition to statutory contributions, the monthly accumulated
amount in the individual retirement account, together with the
compound interest effect, strengthens retirement security.
(b) Tax benefits: Statutory personal contributions and voluntary additional
contributions to retirement and survivor reserves made by public service
personnel are exempt from being included in taxable salary income for
the contribution year.
(c) Submission of applications or changes: Public service personnel must
70

complete the contribution ratio and amount, and sign in person before
the 10th of each month; contributions take effect from the following
month.
c. Self-directed investment:
(a) Starting January 1, 2025, the Public Service Pension Fund Management
Board has launched self-directed investment for public service personnel.
Professional investment advisory firms will be commissioned to design
portfolios with different returns and risks, including conservative, balanced,
aggressive, and lifecycle types, and make them available on the self-directed
investment platform for public service personnel to select portfolios suitable
for their own risk attributes. For those who do not make a selection, the
“lifecycle” portfolio allocated according to different age groups will be used
as the default investment portfolio. Public service personnel may also check
the accumulated results of their individual accounts at any time on the self-
directed investment platform.
(b) Before the 10th of each month, public service personnel may reselect
investment portfolios on the self-directed investment platform. Each year,
there are two (2) fee-free portfolio transfer opportunities.
2. Retirement Eligibility
(1) Voluntary retirement: A faculty member who meets any of the following
conditions may apply for retirement:
a. Having served for five (5) years or more and having reached the age of sixty
(60).
b. Having served for twenty-five (25) years.
(2) Mandatory retirement due to age – applicable persons: A teacher who has
served for five (5) years and has reached the age of sixty-five (65) shall undergo
mandatory retirement due to age.
(3) A retired teacher who has any of the following circumstances shall lose the right
to receive retirement benefits:
a. Death.
b. Deprivation of civil rights for life.
71

c. Conviction by a final conclusive judgment of an offense against the internal or
external security of the State.
d. Loss of the citizenship of the Republic of China (applicable to the defined-
benefit retirement system).
3. Application Time : Four months prior to retirement, complete the teacher
retirement application form and submit it to the department (institute, degree
program, office, center) for processing in accordance with procedures. After
approval by the President, it shall be submitted to the Ministry of Education for
review and determination.
4. Effective Date of Retirement : Where a teacher applies for retirement, except for
special reasons, the effective date of retirement shall be February 1 or August 1.
For those who must retire immediately, where the retirement age is reached
between August 1 and January 31 of the following year, February 1 of the
following year may be used as the effective date of retirement; where the
retirement age is reached between February 1 and July 31, August 1 may be used
as the effective date of retirement.
5. Pension Payment : There are three (3) types: lump-sum pension payment,
monthly pension payment, and receiving one-half (1/2) as lump-sum pension
payment together with one-half (1/2) as monthly pension payment. Where years
of service are less than fifteen years, only the lump-sum pension payment may be
received.
(1) Defined-benefit retirement system: Benefits shall be calculated and paid
according to the retirement benefit calculation basis, the content of the unit’s
base and the standards. Those who receive monthly retirement payments must
meet the statutory starting age for monthly retirement payments or the
transitional indicator number and the basic age.
(2) Individual Pension account (Defined Contribution) retirement system: The lump-
sum retirement payment shall be paid based on the total accumulated amount in
the individual retirement account. There is no age restriction for claiming
monthly retirement payments; however, retirement eligibility conditions must be
met. Monthly retirement payments shall be received by choosing one of the
following based on the total accumulated amount in the individual retirement
72

account: amortized payments (monthly retirement payments calculated by
amortization based on life expectancy and interest rate), fixed-amount payments
(the person selects the monthly amount), or insurance annuity (a one-time
payment at retirement to purchase an annuity insurance that complies with
insurance law requirements).
6. Application to Foreign Professionals : For those subject to the defined-benefit
system, pursuant to Article 23 of the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of
Foreign Professionals, where foreign professional talent is employed as a current,
full-time, qualified, paid teacher within the established staffing system of public
schools in Taiwan and has obtained permanent residence approved by the
National Immigration Agency, Ministry of the Interior, retirement matters shall
apply mutatis mutandis to the retirement provisions for teachers of public
schools, and the person may choose to receive either a lump-sum retirement
payment or a monthly retirement payment. For those subject to the individual
retirement account system, where faculty/staff are foreign nationals only, their
retirement shall apply mutatis mutandis to the provisions of the Act Governing
Retirement, Severance, and Bereavement Compensation Under the Individual
Account System for the Teaching and Other Staff of Public Educational Institutions.
B. Service Extension of Professors
1. General Provision: Based on teaching needs, the University may, upon
recommendation by colleges, departments (institutes, offices, centers, degree

C. Bereavement Compensation
Where a teacher dies of illness or accidental death while in service, or dies due to official
duty, survivor compensation shall be paid to the bereaved family members. Where a
teacher is a foreign national only and dies while in service, the survivor compensation
matters shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Act Governing Retirement, Severance and
survivor compensation for Public School Faculty and Staff and the Act Governing
Retirement, Severance, and Bereavement Compensation Under the Individual Account
System for the Teaching and Other Staff of Public Educational Institutions, and shall be
limited to the payment of a lump-sum compensation payment.
1. Where death is due to illness or accidental death while in service, the survivor
compensation payment method is as follows:
(1) Where years of service are ten years or more but less than fifteen years, a lump-
sum compensation payment shall be paid, and no monthly compensation
payment shall be paid. For each full year of service, 1.5 units (bases) shall be paid;
for any number of months less than 1 year, 1/8 of a unit (base) shall be awarded
per month; any period of less than 1 month shall be calculated as 1 month.
(2) Where years of service are less than ten years, in addition to compensation
payment paid under current regulations, for each month short, an additional
1/12 of a unit (base) shall be added, up to 9 and 11/12 units (bases), after which
no further additions shall be made.
(3) Where years of service are fifteen years or more, a monthly compensation
payment of 1/2 unit (base) shall be paid each month, and a lump-sum
bereavement compensation payment of 15 units (bases) shall be awarded for the
initial fifteen (15) years. For the portion exceeding fifteen (15) years, for each
additional year, an additional 1/2 unit (base) shall be added for each additional
year, up to a maximum of 27 and 1/2 units (bases). For months of service less
than one year, for each month, 1/24 of a unit (base) shall be paid; for less than
one month, it shall be counted as one month. The calculation of the content of
the unit (base) shall be based on the average salary amount listed in the
77

appended table under Article 28, Paragraph 2 of the Act Governing Retirement,
Severance, and Bereavement Compensation for the Teachers and Staff Members
of Public Schools, plus one additional multiple.
2. In accordance with Article 53 of the Act Governing Retirement, Severance, and
Bereavement Compensation for the Teachers and Staff Members of Public Schools
(or Article 40 of the Act Governing Retirement, Severance, and Bereavement
Compensation Under the Individual Account System for the Teaching and Other
Staff of Public Educational Institutions), where death is due to official duty, official-
duty bereavement compensation shall be processed. “Death due to official duty”
refers to death arising from one of the following circumstances, and where the
death has a corresponding causal relationship with such circumstance:
(1) When performing a difficult mission such as disaster response, or performing a
war-related mission, risking one's life and courageously performing the mission
despite facing hazards entailing a high risk of death, resulting in death. While at
the workplace, or while assigned to official travel (duty) to carry out tasks other
than those in the preceding subparagraph, encountering an accident or dangerous
incident, or being subjected to a violent incident, or suffering illness.
(2) The occurrence of an accident or hazard, or an event of violence, or falling prey to
an illness, in the workplace, or while away on official business, when performing a
mission other than one under the preceding paragraph, resulting in death.
(3) Sudden onset of illness, in the workplace, or while away on official business, when
performing a mission other than one under the preceding two subparagraphs.
(4) Any of the following circumstances, resulting in death:
a. The occurrence of an accident or hazard while traveling to or from the
performance of a mission under subparagraph
b. Sudden onset of illness while traveling to or from the performance of a
mission under subparagraph 1 or 2, or the occurrence of an accident or hazard
while traveling to or from the performance of a mission under subparagraph 2.
c. The occurrence of an accident or hazard, or sudden onset of illness, during the
period of advance preparation for the performance of a mission or of follow-
up work after a mission.
78

(5) Unyielding diligence or overwork, resulting in death.
In addition to Bereavement Compensation paid in accordance with regulations, a
lump-sum compensation payment shall be additionally paid. Pursuant to Article
53, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph 1 of the Act Governing Retirement, Severance, and
Bereavement Compensation for the Teachers and Staff Members of Public Schools
(or Article 40, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph 1 of the Act Governing Retirement,
Severance, and Bereavement Compensation Under the Individual Account System
for the Teaching and Other Staff of Public Educational Institutions), for official-duty
Bereavement Compensation due to carrying out arduous tasks such as disaster
(difficulty) rescue, an additional 50% shall be added. For those whose years of
service are less than fifteen years at the time of official-duty death, it shall be
calculated as fifteen years; where years of service are fifteen years or more but
less than twenty-five years, it shall be calculated as twenty-five years for
Bereavement Compensation; where years of service are twenty-five years or more
but less than thirty-five years, it shall be calculated as thirty-five years for
Bereavement Compensation.

D. Reimbursement of Personnel Costs for Research Project Personnel
1. NSTC / Higher Education Sprout Project research personnel
(1) For Postdoctoral Research Fellows remuneration, Full-time Research Personnel
salary, and Project Learning-oriented Assistant learning stipends under NSTC /
Higher Education Sprout Project / Bilingual Learning Program for University
Students (Note: effective May 1, 2024), Office of General Affairs Cashier Section
and the Bilingual & Multilingual Office will compile unified payroll lists. Please
submit the Employment Registration Form and the Research Project
Personnel Appointment Period/Monthly Remuneration Change Application
Form, or the Project Learning-oriented Assistant Change Application Form, to
Personnel Division 4 by the 10th of each month for processing.
(2) The Office of General Affairs Cashier Section compiles unified salary/stipend
lists monthly and remits the previous month’s salary/stipend by the 5th of the
following month. For new personnel (including renewals), payment follows the
payroll schedule depending on onboarding time. Personnel recruited on or after
the 11th of a month (including the 11th) will have the salary/stipend included
and paid in the following month’s payroll.
(3) For part-time project personnel salary, after the PI reviews and approves
attendance records online each month, the employing unit shall compile the
payroll list and process reimbursement monthly. (For instructions, see
Personnel Office website / Personnel Regulations / Project Personnel /
University Regulations: “8. Instructions for Preparing Salary or Learning Stipend
Payroll Lists.”)
2. Non-NSTC research project personnel
(1) Salary/stipend payroll lists for non-NSTC project personnel must be compiled
and reimbursed monthly by the unit, signed by the PI, and after completing the
administrative workflow, remitted in the monthly payroll/stipend payment. (See
the same payroll list instructions cited above.)
(2) For part-time project personnel salary, after the PI reviews and approves
attendance records online monthly, the employing unit compiles and
reimburses the payroll list monthly.
96

(3) Required reimbursement documents: salary/stipend payroll list; funding
approval list (attach approved change notice where applicable). (See payroll list
instructions.)
3. Calculation when not employed for the full month
(1) Salary/stipend = full-month salary/stipend ÷ number of days in the month ×
number of days employed (rounded to the nearest integer).
(2) Premiums: labor insurance and labor pension = full-month premium ÷ 30 × (30
− start date + 1) (rounded to the nearest integer). For NHI, full-month premium
is deducted only if the person remains enrolled at the University on the last day
of the month; otherwise, no deduction is made by the University for that
month.

upon expiry, please log in to “Check Departure Clearance Results” (path: NCCU
website / Faculty & Staff) and print the Online Separation Procedure Form for
Research Project Personnel for doctoral-level research personnel/full-time
project personnel. After the PI signs and relevant units stamp/seal, submit to
